<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

I didn't change `0.html`, because it's already in good shape for what it does: showing a black circle in the middle of the page. It already has:

- **Correct markup:** a doctype, `lang`, charset and viewport tags, and a `<main>` landmark.
- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role="img"` and a labelled `<title>`, and the circle switches to `CanvasText` when the system forces high-contrast colours.
- **Responsive layout:** `min(400px, 90vmin)` sizing, centring with `grid` and `place-items`, and `100dvh` with a `100vh` fallback for mobile browsers.
- **No layout shift:** the SVG has `width`/`height` attributes and a `viewBox`.
- **No extra requests:** the favicon is inlined.

The only small additions I can think of are a `<meta name="description">` tag, or setting `color-scheme` to `light dark` so the page follows dark mode. Whether you want either depends on what the page is for.

What do you want to improve: the look (colour, size, animation), how it behaves, dark mode support, or something else? Tell me and I'll make the change.
